title.en: UDP and TCP: the light one and the steady one
title.zh: UDP 与 TCP：轻的和稳的

description.en: Understand why UDP is only IP plus a port, which applications are willing to give up reliability, and how TCP uses sequence numbers, cumulative acknowledgements, the handshake, a state machine, windows and timers to turn an unreliable network into a reliable byte stream.
description.zh: 懂得 UDP 为什么只比 IP 多一个端口、什么应用愿意放弃可靠性，以及 TCP 怎样用序号、累计确认、握手、状态机、窗口和计时器把不可靠的网络变成一条可靠的字节流。

name.zh: 用户数据报协议 (UDP, User Datagram Protocol)

name.en: TCP service model and connection features
name.zh: TCP 的服务模型与连接特性 (TCP service model and connection features)
TCP 报文段大小与分片 (segment size and fragmentation)

name.en: Byte sequence numbers, cumulative ACK and reliability
name.zh: 字节序号、累计确认与可靠传输 (sequence numbers, cumulative ACK, reliability)
TCP 报文段头部 (TCP segment header)

name.en: TCP connection establishment: three-way handshake and state machine
name.zh: TCP 连接建立：三次握手与状态机 (TCP three-way handshake and state machine)

name.en: TCP connection release: symmetric release, timers and state machine
name.zh: TCP 连接释放：对称释放、计时器与状态机 (TCP connection release)

name.en: TCP window management and flow control
name.zh: TCP 窗口管理与流量控制 (TCP window management, flow control)
重传计时器 (TCP timer management, SRTT)

description.en: Thinking UDP is a "bad" protocol. It is chosen on purpose, for low overhead or so that the application can control reliability itself.
description.zh: 以为 UDP 是「差」的协议。它是为了低开销、或让应用自己控制可靠性而特意选的。

description.en: Thinking a port can have only one connection. A connection is identified uniquely by a four-tuple, so one server port can have many.
description.zh: 以为一个端口只能有一条连接。连接由四元组唯一确定，同一个服务器端口上可以有很多。

description.en: Thinking TCP preserves message boundaries. Writing twice and reading once is entirely possible.
description.zh: 以为 TCP 保留消息边界。写两次、读一次是完全可能的。

description.en: Thinking the acknowledgement number is the sequence number of the segment just received. It is the next byte expected, and it is cumulative.
description.zh: 以为确认号是「刚收到的那个段的序号」。它是期望收到的下一个字节，而且是累计的。

description.en: Thinking SYN uses no sequence number, so the acknowledgement number is x. SYN takes up one sequence number, so the acknowledgement number is x + 1.
description.zh: 以为 SYN 不占序号，确认号就是 x。SYN 占一个序号，所以确认号是 x + 1。

description.en: Treating LAST ACK as "waiting for all packets to disappear". What it waits for is the acknowledgement of its own FIN.
description.zh: 把 LAST ACK 当成「等所有分组消失」。它等的是自己那个 FIN 的确认。

description.en: Treating flow control and congestion control as the same thing. The former protects the receiver, the latter protects the network.
description.zh: 把流量控制和拥塞控制当成一回事。前者保护接收方，后者保护网络。

description.en: Thinking that with TCP a call is certain to run only once. TCP removes duplicates only within one connection; if the connection breaks and the application resends on a new connection, it can still run twice.
description.zh: 以为用了 TCP，一个调用就一定只会执行一次。TCP 只在一条连接内去重，连接断了、应用换新连接重发，仍可能执行两次。

title.en: A voice call loses a packet
title.zh: 语音通话丢了一个包

prompt.en: You are on a voice call with a friend from your dorm. One sound packet is lost. With TCP, it would hold back the data that arrives afterwards and wait for the lost packet to be resent before handing everything to the application in order. Should this call use TCP or UDP?
prompt.zh: 你在宿舍和朋友语音通话。一个声音包丢了。如果用 TCP，它会把后面到的数据先扣住，等丢的包重发回来再按顺序交给应用。这时通话应该用 TCP 还是 UDP？

label.en: TCP: what is lost should be made up, not a single word can be missing
label.zh: TCP：丢了就应该补回来，一个字都不能少

feedback.en: The resent sound is long out of date, since a conversation is real-time, and TCP would also stall the packets behind it.
feedback.zh: 重发回来的声音早已过时了，对话是实时的，而 TCP 还会卡住后面的包。

label.en: UDP: if it's lost, it's lost; a short gap in the sound doesn't matter, and the whole conversation shouldn't stop for it
label.zh: UDP：丢了就丢了，声音里少一小段无所谓，不能为它让整段对话停下来

label.en: Neither; voice calls can't be done over the Internet
label.zh: 都不行，语音通话没法在互联网上做

feedback.en: They can; voice calls make heavy use of UDP.
feedback.zh: 可以，语音通话大量使用 UDP。

label.en: Both: one sends the first half of the sentence, the other the second half
label.zh: 两个都用，一个发前半句，一个发后半句

feedback.en: There is no such usage; which protocol to choose depends on the needs of the whole application.
feedback.zh: 没有这种用法，选哪个协议要看整个应用的需求。

explain.en: In real-time applications, being on time matters more than being complete. UDP does not resend and does not queue, and the application decides for itself how to make up for losses. This lesson covers the lightest one, UDP, first, then the steady one, TCP.
explain.zh: 实时应用里，「及时」比「完整」更重要。UDP 不重发、不排队，应用想怎么补救自己决定。这一课先讲最轻的 UDP，再讲稳的 TCP。

title.en: UDP: IP plus ports, and almost nothing else
title.zh: UDP：比 IP 多了端口，别的几乎没有

text.en: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) offers segments the same service that IP offers datagrams: **unreliable and connectionless**. It adds very little to the network layer. The header is only **8 bytes**:
text.zh: UDP（User Datagram Protocol，用户数据报协议）对报文段提供的服务，和 IP 对数据报提供的一样：**不可靠、无连接**。它没有给网络层加多少东西。头部只有 **8 字节**：

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='14'><rect width='500' height='120' fill='#fafafa'/><g fill='#fff' stroke='#333'><rect x='10' y='10' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='250' y='10' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='10' y='50' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='250' y='50' width='240' height='40'/></g><g text-anchor='middle'><text x='130' y='35'>Source port</text><text x='370' y='35'>Destination port</text><text x='130' y='75'>Length</text><text x='370' y='75'>Checksum</text><text x='250' y='112'>Each box is 16 bits, 8 bytes in all</text></g></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='14'><rect width='500' height='120' fill='#fafafa'/><g fill='#fff' stroke='#333'><rect x='10' y='10' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='250' y='10' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='10' y='50' width='240' height='40'/><rect x='250' y='50' width='240' height='40'/></g><g text-anchor='middle'><text x='130' y='35'>源端口</text><text x='370' y='35'>目的端口</text><text x='130' y='75'>长度</text><text x='370' y='75'>校验和 checksum</text><text x='250' y='112'>每格 16 位，共 8 字节</text></g></svg>

alt.en: UDP header: source port, destination port, length and checksum, 16 bits each
alt.zh: UDP 头部：源端口、目的端口、长度、校验和各 16 位

items.en: **What it adds over bare IP**: ports. IP can only deliver a packet to a host; with ports it can be handed to a particular process in the host, and several applications can share one IP (the multiplexing from the previous lesson). The destination port lets an arriving segment find its process, and the source port lets the other side know where to reply.
items.zh: **相比裸 IP 多了什么**：端口。IP 只能把包送到主机，有了端口才能交给主机里的某个进程，也才能让多个应用共用一个 IP（上一课的多路复用）。目的端口让到来的段找到进程，源端口让对方知道往哪回。

items.en: **What it lacks**: no retransmission, no ordering, no flow control or congestion control. Its only protection is an **optional checksum**: if the data is found corrupted, it is dropped.
items.zh: **没有的东西**：不重传、不排序、没有流量控制和拥塞控制。唯一的保护是**可选的校验和**，发现数据损坏了就丢掉。

items.en: **Reliability, retransmission and congestion control are all left to the application layer**.
items.zh: **可靠性、重传、拥塞控制，都留给应用层**。

summary.en: What exactly the checksum checks (beyond the slides)
summary.zh: 校验和到底校验什么（超出课件）

text.en: It covers the UDP header and the data (the real calculation also includes a "pseudo-header" that contains the IP addresses). The algorithm: add the whole thing up in 16-bit groups, wrap the carry around and add it again, then invert. The receiver adds it up the same way, and if the result is all ones, there was no error. It can only detect errors, not correct them, and on an error the segment is dropped.
text.zh: 它覆盖 UDP 头部和数据（实际计算还要带上一个包含 IP 地址的「伪头部」）。算法：把整段按 16 位一组相加，进位绕回来再加，最后取反。接收方再同样加一遍，结果全是 1 就说明没出错。它只能发现错，不能改正，错了就丢。

caption.en: Illustrative code that fills in the ellipses of the slides' skeleton: the client calls new and then send directly, with no connection; the server gives a port at new, then loops on receive. Port 9876 is just an example.
caption.zh: 示意代码，补全了课件骨架里的省略号：客户端 new 之后直接 send，不用连接；服务器 new 时给端口，再循环 receive。端口 9876 只是举例。

title.en: Who is willing to give up reliability
title.zh: 谁愿意放弃可靠性

text.en: UDP suits two kinds of application: those that **want low overhead**, and those that **want to control** reliability, ordering, retransmission and timing themselves.
text.zh: UDP 适合两类应用：**要低开销**的，和**想自己控制**可靠性、顺序、重传和时机的。

items.en: **Voice and video calls, online games**: one packet carries only a very short stretch of sound or one picture, and is useless once it is late. By the time a resend arrives, that stretch should long since have played, so it is better to skip it, as the next packet is already on its way.
items.zh: **语音、视频通话、在线游戏**：一个包只管很短的一段声音或一个画面，过期就没用。等它重传回来，那一段早该播完了，不如跳过，下一个包已经在路上了。

items.en: **DNS queries** (Lesson 14): one question and one answer, each a single small packet. With TCP you would first have to handshake, spending one extra round trip before the question can even be sent, which costs more than the question itself; if it is lost, the application simply asks again.
items.zh: **DNS 查询**（第 14 课）：一问一答，各只有一个小包。用 TCP 要先握手，多花一个往返才能把问题发出去，比问题本身还贵；丢了，应用自己重问一次就行。

items.en: **Applications that write their own reliability**: if you want to use your own retransmission and congestion strategy, you don't want to be bound by TCP's fixed way of doing things.
items.zh: **自己写可靠性的应用**：想用自己的重传和拥塞策略，就不想被 TCP 的固定做法管着。

text.en: So UDP is not a "bad TCP" but a different design point: it hands the choice about reliability to the application.
text.zh: 所以 UDP 不是「差的 TCP」，而是另一个设计点：把可靠性的选择权交给应用。

title.en: UDP or TCP: remote procedure calls as an example
title.zh: 选 UDP 还是 TCP：以远程过程调用为例

text.en: A remote procedure call (RPC) lets a client call a function on a remote server, and many implementations let you choose UDP or TCP to carry it. This is a favourite exam topic in past papers, though the slides have no dedicated section on it, and it needs one concept: **idempotent**, meaning that calling the same function several times has the same effect as calling it once.
text.zh: 远程过程调用（RPC, Remote Procedure Call）让客户端调用远程服务器上的函数，很多实现让你选用 UDP 或 TCP 来传。这是历年练习题的考点，课件里没有专门讲，要用到一个概念：**幂等**（idempotent），即同一个调用执行多次，效果和执行一次一样。

rows.en: Look up today's weather, read line 10 of a file
rows.zh: 查今天的天气、读文件的第 10 行

rows.en: Charge 100 yuan, add one more milk tea to an order
rows.zh: 扣款 100 元、给订单加一杯奶茶

rows.en: Calling again charges twice, adds a second milk tea
rows.zh: 再调一次就多扣、多加一杯

rows.en: UDP: on timeout just call again, and it also saves the one round trip to set up a connection and the system's cost of keeping connections
rows.zh: UDP：超时就重调，还省掉建连的一个往返和系统维护连接的开销

rows.en: TCP: duplicate segments are recognised and dropped within one connection, so a resend does not cause a repeated execution
rows.zh: TCP：在一条连接内认出并丢掉重复的段，重发不会造成重复执行

title.en: Beyond the slides: TCP's de-duplication has a boundary
title.zh: 超出课件：TCP 的去重有边界

body.en: TCP removes duplicates only **within one connection** (using the sequence numbers from the previous lesson). If the connection breaks halfway and the application sends the request again on a new connection, TCP does not know it is the same call, and it can still run twice. So for non-idempotent calls, the application still has to be careful after a connection drops.
body.zh: TCP 只在**一条连接内**去重（靠上一课的序号）。如果连接中途断了，应用换一条新连接再发一遍请求，TCP 不知道这是同一个调用，仍可能执行两次。所以不幂等的调用，在连接断掉后还要应用自己小心。

title.en: When to let an RPC use UDP
title.zh: 什么时候让 RPC 走 UDP

prompt.en: The university's course-enrolment system has an RPC: get_room(course), which returns today's classroom for a course and does not change any data. The client can implement this RPC with UDP or TCP. Under what condition would the client prefer UDP? Explain the reason using this function.
prompt.zh: 学校选课系统有一个 RPC：get_room(course)，返回某门课今天的上课教室，不改变任何数据。客户端可以用 UDP 或 TCP 实现这个 RPC。什么条件下客户端更愿意用 UDP？结合这个函数说明理由。

key_points.en: get_room is idempotent: running it several times has the same effect as once, so repeats do no harm
key_points.zh: get_room 是幂等的：执行多次和一次效果一样，重复无害

key_points.en: If no reply arrives, just call again; the transport layer need not guarantee delivery exactly once
key_points.zh: 没收到回复就直接再调一次，不需要传输层保证只交付一次

key_points.en: UDP saves the one round trip needed to set up a TCP connection, and the system's cost of maintaining the connection
key_points.zh: UDP 省掉建立 TCP 连接的一个往返，也省掉系统维护连接的开销

model_answer.en: When the function being called is idempotent. get_room is only a query, so it gives the same result however many times it runs. If the client has waited a while without a reply, it can simply call again, with no harm done. UDP is then the better deal: it saves the one round trip needed to set up a TCP connection, and the operating system's overhead for maintaining a connection.
model_answer.zh: 当被调用的函数是幂等的时候。get_room 只是查询，执行多少次结果都一样，所以如果等了一段时间没收到回复，客户端直接再调一次就行，没有任何害处。这时用 UDP 更划算：省掉建立 TCP 连接需要的一个往返，也省掉操作系统维护连接的开销。

explain.en: The criterion is idempotence. If a resend does no harm, there is no need to pay the cost of setting up and maintaining a connection just to get delivery exactly once.
explain.zh: 判断的依据是幂等性。重发无害，就不必为「只交付一次」付出建连和维护连接的代价。

chapter.zh: 端口与 TCP 的服务

title.en: Port numbers: 0 to 65535

text.en: The transport service access point (TSAP) of both TCP and UDP is the port number: 16 bits, from 0 to 65535, in three ranges:
text.zh: TCP 和 UDP 的传输服务访问点（TSAP）就是端口号，16 位，范围 0 到 65535，分三段：

rows.en: Reserved for common services; servers use fixed ports
rows.zh: 留给常见服务，服务器用固定端口
向 IANA 登记的应用

text.en: Why do servers use fixed, well-known ports? Because a client must know beforehand where to knock: to get a web page it goes to 80, and it cannot first ask the server "which port are you on today?". The client's own port need not be fixed, because nobody has to find it in advance: the system hands out a temporary one from the dynamic ports, and the reply finds its way back using the source port.
text.zh: 为什么服务器用固定的知名端口？因为客户端事先要知道往哪敲门：想上网页就去 80，不可能先去问服务器「你今天在哪个端口」。客户端自己的端口则不必固定，没有人要事先找它：系统从动态端口里临时分一个，回信靠源端口找回来。

title.en: One thing to check in the slides
title.zh: 课件里一处要核对

body.en: The slides write RTSP (streaming control) as 543, but the port IANA assigned to RTSP is 554. When you actually need it, go by the IANA port table.
body.zh: 课件把 RTSP（流媒体控制）写成 543，IANA 分配给 RTSP 的是 554。真正要用的时候以 IANA 端口表为准。

title.en: Which range the browser's port falls in
title.zh: 浏览器的端口落在哪一段

prompt.en: Your browser connects to port 80 of www.unimelb.edu.au, and the system assigns a source port to this connection of the browser. Which range is this source port most likely to fall in? Why can't the web server also just take a temporary port like that?
prompt.zh: 你的浏览器去连 www.unimelb.edu.au 的 80 端口，系统给浏览器这条连接分了一个源端口。这个源端口最可能落在哪一段？为什么 Web 服务器不能也这样临时分一个端口？

label.en: Dynamic ports (49152 to 65535). A client must know the server's port beforehand to connect, so server ports have to be fixed and known to all; nobody needs to find the client beforehand, so it just uses a temporary one
label.zh: 动态端口（49152 到 65535）。客户端必须事先知道服务器的端口才能去连，所以服务器端口得固定、人人知道；没人需要事先找客户端，它临时用一个就行

label.en: Well-known ports (0 to 1023). The browser is a common application too, so the system gives it a well-known port as well
label.zh: 知名端口（0 到 1023）。浏览器也是常见应用，系统给它也分一个知名端口

feedback.en: Well-known ports are reserved for common services on servers. A client's port is temporary and is taken from the dynamic ports.
feedback.zh: 知名端口是留给服务器上的常见服务的。客户端的端口是临时的，从动态端口里取。

label.en: Registered ports (1024 to 49151). Every application must register with IANA, and the browser is no exception
label.zh: 注册端口（1024 到 49151）。每个应用都要向 IANA 登记，浏览器也不例外

feedback.en: What gets registered are services that need a fixed port. A client's temporary port needs neither registering nor being fixed.
feedback.zh: 登记的是需要固定端口的服务。客户端的临时端口不用登记，也不用固定。

label.en: Dynamic ports. The server can take a temporary one too, and the client then looks up that port through DNS
label.zh: 动态端口。服务器同样可以临时分一个，客户端再用 DNS 查出这个端口

feedback.en: DNS only turns names into IP addresses and does not give ports. If the server changed ports temporarily, the client would have no way of knowing.
feedback.zh: DNS 只把名字变成 IP 地址，并不给端口。服务器若临时换端口，客户端就无处得知。

explain.en: Behind the division of port ranges is a division of labour: a server must be found, so it uses a fixed well-known port; a client is only the initiator, so it uses a dynamic port, and the reply finds its way back using the source port.
explain.zh: 端口分段背后是分工：服务器要被人找到，所以用固定的知名端口；客户端只是发起方，用动态端口，回信靠源端口找回来。

title.en: TCP: a reliable byte stream on an unreliable network
title.zh: TCP：在不可靠的网络上给一条可靠的字节流

text.en: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented service that provides an end-to-end **reliable byte stream**: segments that arrive out of order are reassembled in order, lost ones are retransmitted, duplicates are dropped, and corrupted ones (detected by the checksum) are dropped. It also looks after **efficiency**: flow control and congestion control.
text.zh: TCP（Transmission Control Protocol）是面向连接的服务，提供端到端**可靠的字节流**：报文段乱序了会按序重组，丢了会重传，重复的丢掉，损坏的（靠校验和发现）丢掉。另外还管**效率**：流量控制和拥塞控制。

text.en: The sender's TCP cuts the byte stream handed over by the process into TCP segments and gives them to IP; the receiver's TCP, on receiving them, reorders them if necessary, restores the byte stream and hands it to the process. Both sides create a socket bound to an IP address and a port, and with TCP a connection must be set up explicitly first.
text.zh: 发送方的 TCP 把进程交来的字节流切成 TCP 报文段交给 IP；接收方的 TCP 收到后，必要时重新排序，还原字节流再交给进程。双方各建一个绑定了 IP 地址和端口的套接字，用 TCP 必须先显式地建立连接。

text.en: A server can have many TCP connections at once on the **same port**. How are they told apart? A connection is identified uniquely by a **four-tuple**: (source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port). The slides' example:
text.zh: 一台服务器可以在**同一个端口**上同时有很多条 TCP 连接。怎么区分？一条连接由一个**四元组**唯一确定：（源 IP，源端口，目的 IP，目的端口）。课件的例子：

text.en: One browser opens two tabs, and both connect to port 80 of the same web server. The server has only one port 80, but the **source ports differ**, so they are two connections.
text.zh: 同一个浏览器开了两个标签页，都连同一个网页服务器的 80 端口。服务器只有一个端口 80，但**源端口不同**，所以是两条连接。

title.en: A byte stream, not a message stream
title.zh: 字节流，不是消息流

text.en: A TCP connection has a few properties: it is **full duplex** (both directions at the same time), **point-to-point** (exactly one sender and one receiver), and a **byte stream**.
text.zh: TCP 连接有几个特性：**全双工**（full duplex，两个方向同时传）、**点到点**（point-to-point，恰好一对发送方和接收方）、**字节流**。

text.en: Being a byte stream means TCP does not preserve message boundaries. If the sender writes 100 bytes and then 200 bytes in two writes, the receiver may get 300 bytes in a single read, or 150 in the first read and 150 in the second. TCP guarantees that the bytes are **in order and not lost**, but not that you read as many times as you wrote. If you need boundaries, the application agrees on them within the data (for example by sending the length first).
text.zh: 字节流的意思是：TCP 不保留消息边界。发送方分两次写 100 字节和 200 字节，接收方可能一次就读到 300 字节；也可能第一次读到 150，第二次读到 150。TCP 保证字节**按序、不丢**，但不保证你写几次就读几次。需要边界，应用自己在数据里约定（比如先发长度）。

text.en: TCP also has a **buffering** option: for efficiency, TCP can hold data back for a moment and then send one big segment, so that the network isn't full of small segments carrying one or two bytes, each lugging a 20-byte header. The cost is **delay**: your data may have to wait a while before being sent. Applications that need immediacy (such as typing on a remote keyboard) can set `TCP_NODELAY` (in Java, `Socket.setTcpNoDelay(true)`) so that data is sent at once.
text.zh: TCP 还有一个**缓冲**的选项：为了效率，TCP 可以先攒一攒，再把一个大段发出去，避免满网络都是装着一两个字节的小报文段，每个小段都要背着 20 字节头部。代价是**延迟**：你的数据可能要等一会儿才发。需要即时的应用（比如远程敲键盘）可以设置 `TCP_NODELAY`（Java 里是 `Socket.setTcpNoDelay(true)`），让数据马上发。

title.en: Another port 4754 turns up
title.zh: 又来了一个端口 4754

prompt.en: The browser on host 128.42.11.3 is already connected to port 80 of 62.118.44.12 using source port 4754. Now the browser on another host, 9.9.9.9, happens to use source port 4754 as well to connect to port 80 of the same server. What will the server treat them as?
prompt.zh: 主机 128.42.11.3 的浏览器已经用源端口 4754 连着 62.118.44.12 的 80 端口。现在另一台主机 9.9.9.9 的浏览器也碰巧用源端口 4754 连同一个服务器的 80 端口。服务器会把它们当成什么？

label.en: Two different connections, because the source IP in the four-tuple is different
label.zh: 两条不同的连接，因为四元组里的源 IP 不同

label.en: The same connection, because the source port and destination port are both the same
label.zh: 同一条连接，因为源端口和目的端口都一样

feedback.en: A connection is identified by the four-tuple, not by the ports alone. A different source IP means a different connection.
feedback.zh: 连接由四元组确定，不是只看端口。源 IP 不同，就是不同的连接。

label.en: A conflict: the second is refused because port 4754 is already taken
label.zh: 冲突，第二条会被拒绝，因为端口 4754 已被占用

feedback.en: Source port 4754 is taken only on host 128.42.11.3, which has no effect on another host.
feedback.zh: 源端口 4754 只是在 128.42.11.3 那台主机上被占用，对另一台主机没影响。

label.en: It depends on which arrives first
label.zh: 不一定，要看哪一个先到

feedback.en: The server tells connections apart by four-tuple, not by order of arrival.
feedback.zh: 服务器按四元组区分，不看到达先后。

explain.en: The four-tuple is (source IP, source port, destination IP, destination port). If any one item differs, it is another connection.
explain.zh: 四元组是（源 IP，源端口，目的 IP，目的端口）。只要有一项不同就是另一条连接。

title.en: How much can one segment carry at most
title.zh: 一个报文段最大能装多少

intro.en: If a segment is too big, then on Ethernet it will be cut into several pieces by IP (fragmentation), and if one piece is lost, the whole segment has to be redone. So we want it to just fit. A TCP segment is a 20-byte header plus zero or more data bytes, and there are two upper limits, whichever is reached first.
intro.zh: 报文段太大，到了以太网会被 IP 切成几片（分片，fragmentation），一片丢了整个报文段就得重来。所以希望它刚好装得下。TCP 报文段是 20 字节头部加 0 个或多个数据字节，有两个上限，要看哪个先到。

why.en: An IPv4 packet is at most 65,535 bytes in total; subtract the 20-byte IP header, and what is left is the packet payload, which is the maximum size of one TCP segment.
why.zh: IPv4 分组总长最多 65,535 字节，里面要扣掉 20 字节 IP 头，剩下的是分组载荷，也就是一个 TCP 报文段的最大尺寸。

why.en: An Ethernet frame payload is generally at most 1500 bytes; subtract the 20-byte IP header and the 20-byte TCP header, and what is left is the data that fits.
why.zh: 以太网帧载荷一般最大 1500 字节，要再扣掉 20 字节 IP 头和 20 字节 TCP 头，才是能装的数据。

outro.en: In practice the value is usually chosen so that the IP header plus the TCP segment just fits in Ethernet's 1500 bytes, avoiding IP fragmentation on the way (Lesson 8). Each segment carries at most 1460 bytes of data; this number is called the MSS (maximum segment size), and when a connection is set up, TCP uses an option for the two ends to tell each other.
outro.zh: 实际取值通常让「IP 头加 TCP 报文段」刚好放进以太网的 1500 字节，避免在路上被 IP 分片（第 8 课）。每个报文段最多装 1460 字节数据，这个数字叫 MSS（最大报文段长度），TCP 建连时用一个选项让两端互相告知。

title.en: Why not 65,515
title.zh: 为什么不是 65,515

prompt.en: The whole path between two hosts is Ethernet (frame payload at most 1500 bytes), and the IP header and TCP header are both 20 bytes. How many bytes of data does TCP normally let each segment carry at most, so that it won't be fragmented by IP?
prompt.zh: 两台主机之间的路径全是以太网（帧载荷最大 1500 字节），IP 头和 TCP 头都是 20 字节。TCP 通常让每个报文段最多装多少字节的数据，才不会被 IP 分片？

explain.en: The 65,515 bytes that IPv4 allows is a theoretical limit, but on the Ethernet along the path one frame holds only 1500 bytes. For the IP header plus the TCP segment to fit, the data is at most $1500-20-20=1460$ bytes, and that is the MSS.
explain.zh: IPv4 允许的 65,515 字节是理论上限，但路径上以太网一帧只能装 1500 字节。要让「IP 头加 TCP 报文段」放进去，数据最多 $1500-20-20=1460$ 字节，这就是 MSS。

hints.en: Start with the Ethernet frame payload of 1500 bytes, then subtract the two headers.
hints.zh: 先看以太网帧载荷 1500 字节，再扣掉两个头。

title.en: Sequence numbers and cumulative acknowledgements: every byte is numbered
title.zh: 序号与累计确认：每个字节都有编号

text.en: TCP numbers **every byte**. The sequence number in a segment is the number of the **first data byte** in that segment. The acknowledgement number is the number of the **next byte expected**, and it is **cumulative** (cumulative ACK): it says "I have received all bytes before this number".
text.zh: TCP 给**每个字节**编号。报文段里的序号，是这个段里**第一个数据字节**的编号。确认号是**期望收到的下一个字节**的编号，而且是**累计**的（cumulative ACK）：它说「这个编号之前的字节我都收到了」。

text.en: A numerical example: the sender cuts the data into segments of 1000 bytes.
text.zh: 数字例子：发送方把数据切成每段 1000 字节。

head.en: Acknowledgement number the receiver sends back
head.zh: 收到后接收方回的确认号

text.en: The starting sequence number is not fixed at 0; each end picks one when the connection is set up (the previous lesson explained why: to keep old segments from colliding with a new connection). Here we treat it as starting from 0 to make the arithmetic easy.
text.zh: 起始序号不是固定从 0 开始，而是建连时两端各选一个（上一课讲过原因：避免旧报文段撞上新连接）。这里为了好算，当作从 0 开始。

items.en: **Loss**: segment 2 is lost. The receiver gets segment 3, but the acknowledgement number is still 1000 (it can only say everything before 1000 has arrived); the sender never receives an acknowledgement for 1000 to 1999, and when the timer expires it retransmits segment 2.
items.zh: **丢失**：第 2 段丢了。接收方收到第 3 段，但确认号仍然是 1000（只能说 1000 之前都收到了），发送方迟迟收不到对 1000 到 1999 的确认，计时器到期后重传第 2 段。

items.en: **Reordering**: the receiver buffers segment 3, which arrived first, and when the missing segment 2 arrives, it assembles them by sequence number, and the acknowledgement number jumps straight to 3000.
items.zh: **乱序**：接收方把先到的第 3 段缓存起来，等缺的第 2 段到了，按序号拼好，确认号一下跳到 3000。

items.en: **Duplication**: if a segment arrives whose sequence number has already been received, it is simply dropped.
items.zh: **重复**：看到序号已经收过的段，直接丢掉。

text.en: The advantage of cumulative acknowledgement is simplicity: one number is enough, and even if some acknowledgements are lost, a later one can cover for them. The limitation is that it can only describe the part received **contiguously**; when a piece is missing, it stops there, even if a lot has arrived after it.
text.zh: 累计确认的好处是简单：一个数就够了，哪怕有些确认丢了，后面的确认也能顶上。局限是：它只能说明**连续**收到的部分，缺了一段就停在那里，哪怕后面的收到了很多。

title.en: Segment 2 is lost: what is the acknowledgement number
title.zh: 第 2 段丢了，确认号是多少

prompt.en: The sender sends three segments with sequence numbers 0, 1000 and 2000, 1000 bytes each. Segment 2 (sequence number 1000) is lost on the way, and segments 1 and 3 both arrive. When the receiver gets segment 3, what acknowledgement number will it send back?
prompt.zh: 发送方发出三个报文段，序号 0、1000、2000，每个 1000 字节。第 2 段（序号 1000）在路上丢了，第 1、3 段都到了。接收方收到第 3 段时，会回的确认号是多少？

explain.en: The acknowledgement number is the next byte expected, and it is cumulative: 0 to 999 have all arrived, but 1000 is missing, so it can only say "expecting 1000", even though 2000 to 2999 has already arrived. When the sender sees the acknowledgement number stuck at 1000, it knows the piece starting at 1000 must be retransmitted.
explain.zh: 确认号是期望的下一个字节，且累计：0 到 999 都收到了，但 1000 缺了，所以只能说「期望 1000」，哪怕后面的 2000 到 2999 已经到了。发送方看到确认号一直是 1000，就知道 1000 开始的那段要重传。

hints.en: The acknowledgement number can only describe the part received contiguously.
hints.zh: 确认号只能说连续收到的部分。

title.en: When to let an RPC use TCP
title.zh: 什么时候让 RPC 走 TCP

prompt.en: The same system has another RPC: pay(account, 50), which records a 50-yuan tuition payment to an account. The client can implement it with UDP or TCP. Under what condition would the client prefer TCP? Give the reason, and point out what TCP helps with here and what its boundary is.
prompt.zh: 同一个系统里还有一个 RPC：pay(account, 50)，把一笔 50 元学费记入账户。客户端可以用 UDP 或 TCP 实现。什么条件下客户端更愿意用 TCP？说明理由，并指出 TCP 这里帮了什么、有什么边界。

key_points.en: pay is not idempotent: running it twice would record 50 yuan extra, so repeated execution is harmful
key_points.zh: pay 不幂等：执行两次会多记 50 元，重复执行有害

key_points.en: TCP uses sequence numbers to detect and discard duplicate segments, so a request resent within one connection is delivered only once
key_points.zh: TCP 用序号发现并丢弃重复的报文段，一条连接内重发的请求只会被交付一次

key_points.en: Boundary: TCP removes duplicates only within one connection; if the connection breaks and the request is resent on a new connection, it can still run twice, so the application must still be careful
key_points.zh: 边界：TCP 只在一条连接内去重，连接断了、换新连接重发仍可能执行两次，应用要自己小心

model_answer.en: Use TCP when the function is not idempotent. pay run twice records 50 yuan extra, so we cannot rely on "no reply, so call again". TCP numbers every byte and drops a repeated sequence number, so a request resent within the same connection is delivered only once and not executed twice. But this holds only within one connection: if the connection breaks and the application resends on a new one, TCP cannot tell it is the same call, so it may still run twice, and the application has to be careful itself.
model_answer.zh: 当函数不幂等时用 TCP。pay 执行两次会多记 50 元，所以不能靠「没收到回复就再调一次」。TCP 给每个字节编号，发现重复的序号就丢掉，所以在同一条连接里重发的请求只会交付一次，不会重复执行。不过这只在一条连接内成立：如果连接断了、应用换一条新连接重发，TCP 认不出这是同一个调用，仍可能执行两次，应用还得自己小心。

explain.en: A non-idempotent call fears repetition, and TCP's sequence-number de-duplication is exactly the cure. Its boundary is a single connection; resending after a connection drops is the application's responsibility.
explain.zh: 不幂等就怕重复，TCP 的序号去重正好对症。它的边界是一条连接内，连接断了之后的重发要由应用负责。

title.en: Sliding window: don't send one and wait for one
title.zh: 滑动窗口：不是发一个等一个

text.en: If you send one segment and wait for its acknowledgement, the network is empty most of the time. The **sliding window** strategy lets the sender have **several segments on the way at once**: each time one is sent, a timer is started; the receiver replies with an acknowledgement and the window size it can still accept; if a timer expires first, the original segment is retransmitted. The window slides forward as acknowledgements arrive.
text.zh: 如果发一个段就等它的确认，网络大部分时间是空的。**滑动窗口**（sliding window）策略让发送方可以**同时有多个报文段在路上**：每发一个就启动计时器；接收方回确认和还能接收的窗口大小；计时器先到期，就重传原来的报文段。窗口随确认往前滑。

alt.zh: 字节序列上，已确认的、已发未确认的、窗口内可发的、窗口外的四段，窗口覆盖已发未确认和可发的部分

caption.en: The window is a contiguous range of bytes, and its left edge is the first byte not yet acknowledged.
caption.zh: 窗口是一段连续的字节范围，左边界是第一个还没被确认的字节。

text.zh: 好处算给你看（忽略发送本身所需的时间）。往返一次 100 ms，每段 1000 字节：

text.en: On the same line, opening the window to 4 segments makes the speed 4 times as high. How wide the window can open is limited jointly by the receiver's buffer space and the congestion in the network, as we will see later.
text.zh: 同样的线路，窗口开到 4 段，速度就是 4 倍。窗口开多大，由接收方的缓冲空间和网络的拥塞情况共同限制，后面会讲。

title.zh: TCP 头部：每个字段为什么需要

caption.en: Each row is 32 bits, and the fixed part is 20 bytes in all.
caption.zh: 每行 32 位，固定部分共 20 字节。

items.en: **Source and destination ports**: the endpoints at the two ends of this connection, two of the items in the four-tuple.
items.zh: **源、目的端口**：这条连接两端的端点，四元组里的两项。

items.en: **Sequence number and acknowledgement number**: the byte numbering and cumulative acknowledgement from the previous page.
items.zh: **序号、确认号**：上一页讲的字节编号和累计确认。

items.en: **Header length**: in units of 32-bit words (4 bytes). A value of 5 means 20 bytes (no options), and 8 means 32 bytes (with 12 bytes of options). Because the options vary in length, the receiver needs this to know where the data starts.
items.zh: **头部长度**：以 32 位字（4 字节）为单位。写 5 就是 20 字节（没有选项），写 8 就是 32 字节（带 12 字节选项）。因为选项长度可变，接收方要靠它知道数据从哪开始。

items.en: **Window size**: counting from the acknowledged byte, how many more bytes may be sent (covered later).
items.zh: **窗口大小**：从已确认的字节算起，还允许再发多少字节（后面讲）。

items.en: **Checksum**: covers the header and the data, to detect corruption.
items.zh: **校验和**：覆盖头部和数据，发现损坏。

items.en: **Options**: extra functions, such as the maximum segment size MSS, timestamps and selective acknowledgement SACK.
items.zh: **选项**：额外的功能，例如最大报文段长度 MSS、时间戳、选择确认 SACK。

text.en: The most commonly used **flags**:
text.zh: 最常用的几个**标志位**：

rows.en: The acknowledgement number is valid; if 0, the acknowledgement number is ignored
rows.zh: 确认号有效；0 则忽略确认号

rows.en: Set up a connection. A connection request has SYN = 1, ACK = 0; a connection reply has SYN = 1, ACK = 1 (it also acknowledges the other side's SYN)
rows.zh: 建立连接。连接请求 SYN = 1、ACK = 0；连接应答 SYN = 1、ACK = 1（它顺带确认了对方的 SYN）

rows.en: The sender has no more data to send and closes this direction, but can still receive
rows.zh: 发送方没有数据要发了，关闭这个方向，但仍可以接收

rows.en: Abruptly reset a confused connection; also used to reject an invalid segment or to refuse a connection
rows.zh: 突然重置一条混乱的连接，也用来拒绝无效的段或拒绝建连

items.en: **PSH**: asks the receiver to hand the data to the application as soon as it arrives, without buffering.
items.zh: **PSH**：要求接收方一到就交给应用，别缓冲。

items.en: **URG**: the urgent pointer is valid, and the pointer says where the urgent data is, counting from the current sequence number; rarely used nowadays.
items.zh: **URG**：紧急指针有效，指针给出从当前序号起紧急数据在哪里；现在很少用。

items.en: **ECE, CWR**: send a congestion signal when explicit congestion notification (ECN) is used. When the receiver receives a congestion indication from the network, it uses ECE to tell the sender to slow down; after slowing down, the sender uses CWR to tell the receiver it can stop sending ECE. Congestion control comes in Lesson 13.
items.zh: **ECE、CWR**：用显式拥塞通知（ECN）时发出拥塞信号。接收方收到网络的拥塞提示，用 ECE 告诉发送方放慢；发送方放慢后用 CWR 告诉接收方可以停止回 ECE。拥塞控制第 13 课再讲。

title.en: Header length = 7
title.zh: 头部长度 = 7

prompt.en: The "header length" field of a TCP segment header has the value 7. How many bytes is this header in all? How many of them are options?
prompt.zh: 一个 TCP 报文段头部的「头部长度」字段值是 7。这个头部一共多少字节？其中选项占多少字节？

label.en: 28 bytes, of which options are 8 bytes
label.zh: 28 字节，其中选项占 8 字节

label.en: 7 bytes, of which options are 0 bytes
label.zh: 7 字节，其中选项占 0 字节

feedback.en: The unit of header length is the 32-bit word (4 bytes), not the byte, and the fixed part alone is 20 bytes.
feedback.zh: 头部长度的单位是 32 位字（4 字节），不是字节，而且固定部分就有 20 字节。

label.en: 28 bytes, of which options are 28 bytes
label.zh: 28 字节，其中选项占 28 字节

feedback.en: 28 bytes is the whole header, which first has a 20-byte fixed part; the options are only the extra part.
feedback.zh: 28 字节是整个头部，里面先有 20 字节的固定部分，选项只是多出来的那部分。

label.en: 35 bytes, of which options are 15 bytes
label.zh: 35 字节，其中选项占 15 字节

feedback.en: A word is 4 bytes, not 5. Seven words are 28 bytes.
feedback.zh: 一个字是 4 字节，不是 5 字节。7 个字是 28 字节。

explain.en: Seven 32-bit words are $7\times4=28$ bytes; subtracting the fixed 20 bytes, the options take 8 bytes. The data starts after byte 28, and the receiver finds it by exactly this field.
explain.zh: 7 个 32 位字就是 $7\times4=28$ 字节，减去固定的 20 字节，选项占 8 字节。数据从第 28 个字节之后开始，接收方正是靠这个字段找到它。

chapter.en: Birth and death of a connection

title.en: TCP's three-way handshake: why SYN takes up a sequence number
title.zh: TCP 的三次握手：SYN 为什么占一个序号

text.en: This is the TCP version of the previous lesson's three-way handshake. The server first does LISTEN, and the client does CONNECT:
text.zh: 这就是上一课三次握手的 TCP 版本。服务器先 LISTEN，客户端 CONNECT：

alt.en: TCP three-way handshake: SYN seq=x; SYN+ACK seq=y ack=x+1; ACK seq=x+1 ack=y+1; each side's state is marked beside it
alt.zh: TCP 三次握手：SYN seq=x；SYN+ACK seq=y ack=x+1；ACK seq=x+1 ack=y+1；两侧标出各自的状态

caption.en: The two sides show their own states: the client goes CLOSED, SYN SENT, ESTABLISHED; the server goes LISTEN, SYN RCVD, ESTABLISHED.
caption.zh: 两侧是各自的状态：客户端 CLOSED、SYN SENT、ESTABLISHED；服务器 LISTEN、SYN RCVD、ESTABLISHED。

text.en: The slides don't mark flags on the third segment: it has only the ACK bit set to 1 (SYN is 0) and normally carries no data, so it is a pure ACK.
text.zh: 第三个段课件没标标志位：它只有 ACK 位为 1（SYN 为 0），通常不带数据，所以是一个纯 ACK。

text.en: Why is the acknowledgement number x + 1 and not x? Because although SYN carries no data, it **takes up one sequence number**. That way it too can be acknowledged and is not confused with the data that follows. An acknowledgement number of x + 1 means "I received your SYN (sequence number x), and the next one I expect is x + 1", so the client's first data byte has sequence number x + 1. FIN likewise takes up one sequence number.
text.zh: 为什么确认号是 x + 1，不是 x？因为 SYN 虽然不带数据，却**占一个序号**。这样它也能被确认，不会和后面的数据混淆。确认号 x + 1 的意思是「你的 SYN（序号 x）我收到了，下一个我期望 x + 1」，所以客户端的第一个数据字节序号是 x + 1。FIN 同样占一个序号。

text.en: **Simultaneous open**: two hosts happen to send SYN to each other at the same moment. Step by step:
text.zh: **同时打开**（simultaneous open）：两台主机恰好同时向对方发 SYN。一步步走：

items.en: Both send SYN (A's seq = x, B's seq = y) and both enter SYN SENT.
items.zh: 双方都发出 SYN（A 的 seq = x，B 的 seq = y），都进入 SYN SENT。

items.en: A receives B's SYN and replies SYN + ACK (ack = y + 1), entering SYN RCVD; B likewise receives A's SYN, replies SYN + ACK (ack = x + 1), and also enters SYN RCVD.
items.zh: A 收到 B 的 SYN，回 SYN + ACK（ack = y + 1），进入 SYN RCVD；B 同样收到 A 的 SYN，回 SYN + ACK（ack = x + 1），也进入 SYN RCVD。

items.en: A receives B's SYN + ACK, which acknowledges A's own SYN, and A enters ESTABLISHED; B does the same.
items.zh: A 收到 B 的 SYN + ACK，它确认了 A 自己的 SYN，A 进入 ESTABLISHED；B 同理。

text.en: The attempts in the two directions use the same four-tuple, which for TCP is the same connection, so only **one** connection results.
text.zh: 两个方向的尝试用的是同一个四元组，对 TCP 来说就是同一条连接，所以只会得到**一条**连接。

title.en: Following the sequence numbers of a handshake
title.zh: 追一次握手的序号

prompt.en: The client picks x = 100 and the server picks y = 300. In steps two and three of the three-way handshake, what are (seq, ack) in each?
prompt.zh: 客户端选 x = 100，服务器选 y = 300。三次握手的第二步和第三步里，（seq，ack）各是多少？

label.en: Step two (300, 101); step three (101, 301)
Step two (300, 100); step three (100, 300)

feedback.en: This forgets that SYN takes up a sequence number. The acknowledgement number must be the next sequence number expected, which is x + 1 and y + 1, and the client's next sequence number is also x + 1.
feedback.zh: 忘了 SYN 占一个序号。确认号要写下一个期望的序号，也就是 x + 1 和 y + 1，客户端下一个序号也是 x + 1。

label.en: Step two (300, 101); step three (100, 301)

feedback.en: The client's SYN has already used sequence number 100, so in step three its sequence number is the next one, 101.
feedback.zh: 客户端的 SYN 已经占了序号 100，第三步它的序号是下一个，也就是 101。

label.en: Step two (300, 101); step three (101, 300)

feedback.en: The server's SYN also takes up a sequence number, 300, so when the client acknowledges it, it must write the next expected one, 301.
feedback.zh: 服务器的 SYN 也占一个序号 300，客户端确认它时要写下一个期望的 301。

explain.en: SYN takes up one sequence number: the client's SYN uses up 100, so the server's acknowledgement number is 101 and the client's next segment has sequence number 101; the server's SYN uses up 300, so the client's acknowledgement number is 301.
explain.zh: SYN 占一个序号：客户端 SYN 用掉 100，所以服务器的确认号是 101，客户端下一段的序号也是 101；服务器 SYN 用掉 300，所以客户端的确认号是 301。

hints.en: Every SYN takes up one sequence number, and the acknowledgement number is the "next one expected".
hints.zh: 每一个 SYN 都占一个序号，确认号写的是「下一个期望的」。

title.en: The finite state machine: establishment first, only five states
title.zh: 有限状态机：先看建立，只有五个状态

text.en: TCP describes a connection with a **finite state machine**: at any moment it is in one state, an event makes it move, and a segment may be sent at the same time. There are 11 states in all, and taking them all in at once is dizzying, so we split them into two groups: first the 5 used for establishment, and on the next page the 6 used for release.
text.zh: TCP 用**有限状态机**（finite state machine）描述一条连接：任何时刻处在一个状态，发生一个事件就转移，同时可能发出一个报文段。一共 11 个状态，一次全看会晕，分成两组：先看建立用到的 5 个，下一页再看释放用到的 6 个。

rows.zh: 没有连接，也没有待处理的

rows.en: The server is waiting for someone to connect
The application has started setting up a connection (SYN sent)
rows.zh: 应用已经开始建立连接（SYN 已发）

rows.en: A connection request has arrived, waiting for the ACK
rows.zh: 收到了连接请求，等 ACK

rows.en: The state in which data is transferred normally

alt.en: State diagram of the establishment phase: the client goes from CLOSED via CONNECT/SYN to SYN SENT, then via SYN+ACK/ACK to ESTABLISHED; the server goes from CLOSED via LISTEN to LISTEN, via SYN/SYN+ACK to SYN RCVD, then via ACK to ESTABLISHED; the dotted line is simultaneous open
alt.zh: 建立阶段的状态图：客户端 CLOSED 经 CONNECT/SYN 到 SYN SENT，再经 SYN+ACK/ACK 到 ESTABLISHED；服务器 CLOSED 经 LISTEN 到 LISTEN，经 SYN/SYN+ACK 到 SYN RCVD，再经 ACK 到 ESTABLISHED；点线是同时打开

caption.en: Labels read “event / segment sent”, and “–” means no segment is sent.
caption.zh: 标签写法是「触发 / 发出」，「–」表示不发报文段。

items.en: **Client** (solid): CLOSED; CONNECT sends SYN → SYN SENT; on receiving SYN + ACK it replies ACK → ESTABLISHED.
items.zh: **客户端**（实线）：CLOSED，CONNECT 发 SYN → SYN SENT，收到 SYN + ACK 回 ACK → ESTABLISHED。

items.en: **Server** (dashed): CLOSED; LISTEN → LISTEN; on receiving SYN it replies SYN + ACK → SYN RCVD; on receiving ACK → ESTABLISHED.
items.zh: **服务器**（虚线）：CLOSED，LISTEN → LISTEN，收到 SYN 回 SYN + ACK → SYN RCVD，收到 ACK → ESTABLISHED。

items.en: **Simultaneous open** (dotted): in SYN SENT, the other side's SYN arrives; it replies SYN + ACK and moves straight to SYN RCVD, then waits for the other side's SYN + ACK to acknowledge its own SYN, and reaches ESTABLISHED.
items.zh: **同时打开**（点线）：SYN SENT 里收到对方的 SYN，回 SYN + ACK，直接转到 SYN RCVD，再等对方的 SYN + ACK 确认自己的 SYN，到 ESTABLISHED。

text.en: The point in reading the diagram: the two paths meet at ESTABLISHED, and simultaneous open is a side branch that goes from the client side across to the server side.
text.zh: 看图的要点：两条路径在 ESTABLISHED 汇合，同时打开是从客户端那一侧岔向服务器那一侧的支路。

title.en: Release: each direction closed on its own
title.zh: 释放：每个方向各关各的

text.en: TCP uses **symmetric release** (the previous lesson): each direction is closed separately, **FIN** means "this side has no more data to send", and lost release segments are handled by timers. The remaining 6 states fall into two groups: the **active closer**, which sends FIN first, uses 4, and the **passive closer**, which receives the FIN later, uses 2.
text.zh: TCP 用**对称释放**（symmetric release，上一课）：每个方向单独关，**FIN** 表示「这边没有数据要发了」，丢失的释放报文靠计时器处理。剩下的 6 个状态分成两组：先发 FIN 的**主动关闭方**用 4 个，后收到 FIN 的**被动关闭方**用 2 个。

alt.en: State diagram of the release phase: the active closer goes from ESTABLISHED via CLOSE/FIN to FIN WAIT 1, then FIN WAIT 2, TIME WAIT, CLOSED; FIN WAIT 1 receiving a FIN goes to CLOSING; the passive closer goes via FIN/ACK to CLOSE WAIT, via CLOSE/FIN to LAST ACK, and via ACK to CLOSED
alt.zh: 释放阶段的状态图：主动关闭方 ESTABLISHED 经 CLOSE/FIN 到 FIN WAIT 1，再到 FIN WAIT 2、TIME WAIT、CLOSED；FIN WAIT 1 收到 FIN 到 CLOSING；被动关闭方经 FIN/ACK 到 CLOSE WAIT，CLOSE/FIN 到 LAST ACK，ACK 到 CLOSED

caption.en: The active side (blue) goes around back to CLOSED by way of TIME WAIT; the passive side (orange) is shorter and closes once its own FIN is acknowledged.
caption.zh: 主动方（蓝）绕一圈回到 CLOSED 要经过 TIME WAIT；被动方（橙）短一些，等到自己的 FIN 被确认就关。

rows.en: I'm done on my side, FIN sent, waiting for it to be acknowledged
rows.zh: 我这边说完了，FIN 已发，等它被确认

rows.en: My FIN has been acknowledged, waiting for the other side to close too
rows.zh: 我的 FIN 已被确认，等对方也关

rows.en: Both sides sent FIN almost at the same time, and the other side's FIN arrived first
rows.zh: 双方几乎同时发了 FIN，对方的 FIN 先到了

rows.en: Wait a while so that all leftover packets in the network disappear (next page)
rows.zh: 等一阵，让网络里所有残余的分组消失（下一页讲）

rows.en: The other side closed first, and I can still keep sending
rows.zh: 对方先关了，我这边还可以继续发

rows.en: I have sent my FIN too, and what I wait for is **the acknowledgement of this FIN**
rows.zh: 我也发了 FIN，等的是**这个 FIN 的确认**

items.en: **Active closer**: ESTABLISHED; CLOSE sends FIN → FIN WAIT 1; on receiving ACK → FIN WAIT 2; on receiving the other side's FIN it replies ACK → TIME WAIT; on timeout → CLOSED. If in FIN WAIT 1 the other side's FIN arrives first, it goes to CLOSING, and on receiving ACK to TIME WAIT; if what arrives is FIN + ACK, it goes straight to TIME WAIT.
items.zh: **主动关闭方**：ESTABLISHED，CLOSE 发 FIN → FIN WAIT 1，收到 ACK → FIN WAIT 2，收到对方的 FIN 回 ACK → TIME WAIT，超时 → CLOSED。若在 FIN WAIT 1 里先收到对方的 FIN，就到 CLOSING，再收到 ACK 到 TIME WAIT；若收到的是 FIN + ACK，则直接到 TIME WAIT。

items.en: **Passive closer**: on receiving FIN it replies ACK → CLOSE WAIT; on its own CLOSE it sends FIN → LAST ACK; on receiving ACK → CLOSED.
items.zh: **被动关闭方**：收到 FIN 回 ACK → CLOSE WAIT，自己 CLOSE 发 FIN → LAST ACK，收到 ACK → CLOSED。

title.en: The slides describe LAST ACK and TIME WAIT identically
title.zh: 课件里 LAST ACK 和 TIME WAIT 写成了一样

body.en: The slides' state table writes both as "waiting for all packets to disappear". LAST ACK is actually waiting for **the acknowledgement of its own FIN**; only TIME WAIT is waiting for packets to disappear.
body.zh: 课件的状态表把两个都写成「等所有分组消失」。LAST ACK 其实是在等**自己那个 FIN 的确认**，只有 TIME WAIT 是在等分组消失。

title.en: Which states the active closer goes through
title.zh: 主动关闭方走过哪些状态

prompt.en: A connection in ESTABLISHED, the application executes CLOSE, and the other side responds obediently, with no errors and no simultaneous close. Which states does the actively closing side go through, in order, until CLOSED?
prompt.zh: 一条处于 ESTABLISHED 的连接，应用执行 CLOSE，对方也乖乖回应，没有出错，也没有同时关闭。主动关闭的这一方，依次经过哪些状态直到 CLOSED？

options.label: FIN WAIT 1 → FIN WAIT 2 → TIME WAIT → CLOSED

feedback.en: This is the path of the passive closer: it was closed first by the other side, so it goes to CLOSE WAIT first.
feedback.zh: 这是被动关闭方走的路：它是被对方先关的，所以先到 CLOSE WAIT。

feedback.en: CLOSING happens only when both sides send FIN almost at the same time, and even then it goes through TIME WAIT afterwards and does not go straight to CLOSED.
feedback.zh: CLOSING 只在双方几乎同时发 FIN 时才有，而且它之后还要经过 TIME WAIT，不会直接到 CLOSED。

feedback.en: This leaves out TIME WAIT. After sending the last ACK, the active closer waits a while before it closes.
feedback.zh: 漏了 TIME WAIT。主动关闭方回完最后的 ACK 后还要等一阵才关。

explain.en: Active side: sending FIN takes it to FIN WAIT 1, the FIN being acknowledged takes it to FIN WAIT 2, receiving the other side's FIN and replying ACK takes it to TIME WAIT, and after waiting a while it times out to CLOSED. The passive side goes through CLOSE WAIT and LAST ACK, a shorter road.
explain.zh: 主动方：发 FIN 进 FIN WAIT 1，FIN 被确认进 FIN WAIT 2，收到对方的 FIN 并回 ACK 进 TIME WAIT，等一阵超时后 CLOSED。被动方走 CLOSE WAIT 和 LAST ACK，路更短。

title.en: TIME WAIT: why wait after sending the last ACK
title.zh: TIME WAIT：为什么回完最后一个 ACK 还要等

text.en: Why doesn't the active closer close right after sending the last ACK, instead of staying in TIME WAIT for a while (implementations usually use twice the maximum segment lifetime; the slides give no number)? There are two reasons:
text.zh: 主动关闭方回完最后那个 ACK，为什么不马上关，要在 TIME WAIT 里待一阵（实现里一般取最大报文段寿命的两倍，课件没给数字）？有两个原因：

items.en: **The last ACK may be lost.** The passive side, in LAST ACK, gets no acknowledgement and resends its FIN. If the active side has already closed, nobody can reply with an ACK; staying in TIME WAIT, it can still reply once more.
items.zh: **最后那个 ACK 可能丢。**被动方在 LAST ACK 里等不到确认，会重发 FIN。如果主动方已经关了，没人能再回 ACK；留在 TIME WAIT，就还能再回一次。

items.en: **Old, delayed segments could pose as a new connection.** A connection is identified by its four-tuple; if a new connection with the same four-tuple is set up straight away, an old segment from the previous connection that happens to arrive late could be accepted by the new one. After waiting one or two segment lifetimes, the old segments have all disappeared.
items.zh: **旧的、延迟的报文段会冒充新连接。**连接用四元组标识，如果马上又建一条同样四元组的新连接，上一条连接的旧报文段恰好迟到，就可能被新连接收下。等上一两倍的报文段寿命，旧段都已消失。

text.en: This is the same thing as the two-army problem from the previous lesson: the last message can always be lost, and no protocol can let both sides know for certain that the other received it. TCP's answer is also the same as in the previous lesson: use timers to **bring the risk down**, not to eliminate it.
text.zh: 这和上一课的两军问题是一回事：最后一条消息总有丢的可能，没有协议能让双方确凿地知道对方收到了。TCP 的做法也和上一课一样：靠计时器把风险**压低**，而不是消灭。

title.en: If the last ACK is lost
title.zh: 如果最后的 ACK 丢了

prompt.en: The actively closing side sends the last ACK, and suppose it does not enter TIME WAIT but closes the connection at once, and this ACK happens to be lost on the way. What happens next?
prompt.zh: 主动关闭的一方回完最后的 ACK，假设它不进 TIME WAIT，立刻关闭了连接，而这个 ACK 恰好在路上丢了。接下来会怎样？

label.en: The passive side, in LAST ACK, gets no acknowledgement and resends its FIN, but the active side no longer has this connection and cannot reply with an ACK
label.zh: 被动方在 LAST ACK 里等不到确认，会重发 FIN，但主动方已没有这条连接，没法再回 ACK

label.en: The passive side assumes its FIN has been acknowledged and goes straight to CLOSED, with no problem at all
label.zh: 被动方认为自己的 FIN 已经被确认，直接进入 CLOSED，什么问题也没有

feedback.en: Without receiving the ACK, it will not assume the FIN has been acknowledged. LAST ACK is waiting for exactly the acknowledgement of its own FIN.
feedback.zh: 没收到 ACK，它就不会认为 FIN 被确认。LAST ACK 等的正是自己那个 FIN 的确认。

label.en: The passive side resends FIN, and on receiving it the active side automatically sets up a new connection
label.zh: 被动方重发 FIN，主动方收到后会自动重新建立一条连接

feedback.en: A closed connection does not come back to life by itself; setting up a new connection takes a new handshake.
feedback.zh: 关闭了的连接不会自己复活，建立新连接要重新握手。

label.en: The resent FIN from the passive side is dropped by routers, because routers know the connection has ended
label.zh: 被动方重发的 FIN 会被路由器丢弃，因为路由器认得这条连接已结束

feedback.en: Routers are stateless, do not know about connections, and do not drop segments on behalf of the endpoints.
feedback.zh: 路由器无状态，不认识连接，也不会替端点丢弃报文段。

explain.en: This is the first reason for TIME WAIT: by keeping the connection around for a while, a lost last ACK can be sent again. With a timer, TCP brings this two-army kind of risk down to an acceptable level.
explain.zh: 这就是 TIME WAIT 的第一个理由：留着连接一阵，丢了的最后一个 ACK 才能补发。靠计时器，TCP 把这个两军问题式的风险压低到可以接受。

hints.en: Think about what the passive side is waiting for in LAST ACK.
hints.zh: 想想被动方在 LAST ACK 里等的是什么。

title.en: Window management: the receiver says how much more it can hold
title.zh: 窗口管理：接收方说「我还能装多少」

text.en: The receiver's buffer is limited. If the sender sends faster than the application reads, the buffer will overflow. So the receiver **advertises a window** in every acknowledgement: according to the **space remaining** in its buffer, it tells the sender "you may send at most this much more". This is **flow control**.
text.zh: 接收方的缓冲区是有限的。如果发送方发得比应用读得快，缓冲区就会溢出。所以接收方在每个确认里**通告窗口**（advertised window）：按自己缓冲区**剩余的空间**，告诉发送方「你最多还能再发这么多」。这就是**流量控制**（flow control）。

text.en: The slides' example: the receiver's buffer is 4 KB. The bar on the right is the receive buffer, and the grey part is the occupied portion.
text.zh: 课件的例子：接收方缓冲区 4 KB。右边的条是接收缓冲区，灰色是已占用的部分。

alt.en: Timeline of sender and receiver, with the receive buffer on the right filling and emptying with the events: write 2 KB, ACK 2048 WIN 2048; write 2 KB more, buffer full and sender blocked; after the receiving application reads 2 KB, a window update is sent and the sender may send 1 KB more
alt.zh: 发送方与接收方的时序图，右侧是接收缓冲区随事件填满和腾空：写 2 KB，ACK 2048 WIN 2048；再写 2 KB，缓冲区满，发送方被阻塞；接收方应用读走 2 KB 后发窗口更新，发送方可再发 1 KB

caption.en: Each side does its own thing: the write on the left is the sender's application, and the read on the right is the receiver's application.
caption.zh: 发送方和接收方各管各的：左边的写是发送方的应用，右边的读是接收方的应用。

text.en: How to read it: the sender's application writes 2 KB, and on arrival at the receiver the buffer holds 2 KB, so the receiver replies ACK = 2048, WIN = 2048 (the remaining space). The sender's application writes 2 KB more, the buffer is full, the window is 0, and the sender is blocked. After the receiver's application reads 2 KB, the receiver sends a **window update**, the window opens again, and the sender can send up to 2 KB more; in the figure it actually sends 1 KB.
text.zh: 怎么读：发送方应用写 2 KB，到了接收方，缓冲区占 2 KB，接收方回 ACK = 2048、WIN = 2048（剩余空间）。发送方应用再写 2 KB，缓冲区满了，窗口是 0，发送方被阻塞。接收方的应用读走 2 KB 后，接收方发**窗口更新**，窗口重新打开，发送方可以再发最多 2 KB，图里实际发了 1 KB。

title.en: Beyond the slides: what if the window stays at zero
title.zh: 超出课件：窗口一直是零怎么办

body.en: If the window update is lost, the two sides end up waiting for each other: the sender waits for a window, and the receiver waits for data. To guard against this deadlock, when the window is 0 the sender periodically sends a tiny window probe, forcing the receiver to reply with the current window value.
body.zh: 窗口更新万一丢了，会出现互相等待：发送方在等窗口，接收方在等数据。为了防这种死等，发送方在窗口为 0 时会定期发一个很小的窗口探测，逼接收方回一个当前的窗口值。

rows.en: The receiver: don't send faster than it can receive
rows.zh: 接收方：别发得比它收得快

rows.en: The network: don't send so much that routers in the middle clog up
rows.zh: 网络：别发得让中间的路由器堵塞

rows.en: Inferred from how the network behaves (next lesson)
rows.zh: 从网络的表现推断（下一课）

title.en: What is the window
title.zh: 窗口是多少

prompt.en: The receiver's buffer totals 4096 bytes. 3000 bytes have been received and not yet read by the application, and the rest is empty. In the acknowledgement it sends now, what should the window size be, in bytes?
prompt.zh: 接收方缓冲区总共 4096 字节。已经收到 3000 字节还没被应用读走，其余是空的。接收方这时回的确认里，窗口大小应该是多少字节？

explain.en: The window is advertised as the **remaining space** in the buffer: 4096 − 3000 = 1096. After the application reads the data, the remaining space grows, and the window opens again with it.
explain.zh: 窗口按缓冲区**剩余的空间**通告：4096 − 3000 = 1096。应用把数据读走后，剩余空间变大，窗口也随之重新打开。

hints.en: Window = total buffer − space in use.
hints.zh: 窗口 = 总缓冲 − 已占用。

title.en: The retransmission timer: how long to wait before deciding it is lost
title.zh: 重传计时器：等多久才算丢了

intro.en: It is hard to decide how long to set the timer: too early, and the packet is actually still on its way, so it is resent for nothing; too late, and a loss is noticed only after a long time, so reliability costs more. The way out is to **measure** the network's behaviour **dynamically** and let the timer follow: measure the **smoothed round-trip time** SRTT and its **variation**. (The slides only require knowing this idea; the specific formulas below go beyond the slides and are typical values from common implementations.) Suppose the current SRTT = 100 ms, the variation RTTVAR = 10 ms, and a new round trip is measured at R = 140 ms.
intro.zh: 计时器设多长很难：设早了，包其实还在路上，白重发一遍；设晚了，丢了很久才发现，可靠要付出更大代价。办法是**动态测量**网络的表现，计时器跟着调：测量**平滑往返时间** SRTT（smoothed round-trip time）和它的**波动**。（课件只要求知道这个思路，下面的具体公式超出课件，取自常用实现的典型值。）设当前 SRTT = 100 ms，波动 RTTVAR = 10 ms，新测到一次往返 R = 140 ms。

why.en: Smoothing: the new sample takes only a small share, so one chance fluctuation doesn't pull the estimate off.
why.zh: 平滑：新样本只占一小部分，一次偶然的抖动不会把估计带偏。

why.en: Variation: round-trip times go up and down, and the timer must leave enough margin, or a little jitter would be mistaken for a loss. The SRTT used here is the 100 from before the update.
why.zh: 波动：往返时间忽大忽小，计时器要留够余量，否则一点抖动就误判成丢包。这里用的 SRTT 是更新之前的 100。

why.en: The retransmission timeout (RTO) = the average plus a few times the variation. The larger the variation, the longer the wait.
why.zh: 重传超时（RTO）= 平均值加几倍波动。波动越大，等得越久。

outro.en: One more detail: if a segment has been retransmitted, an ACK that arrives afterwards cannot tell whether it acknowledges the first transmission or the resend; this is called **retransmission ambiguity**. Such samples must be skipped when computing RTT, or absurd values result.
outro.zh: 还有一个细节：如果一个报文段被重传过，之后到的 ACK 无法判断是对第一次发的还是对重发的确认，这叫**重传的二义性**。算 RTT 时要跳过这样的样本，否则会算出荒唐的值。

title.en: Computing a retransmission timeout
title.zh: 算一次重传超时

prompt.en: Using the formulas above: the current SRTT = 80 ms, RTTVAR = 4 ms, and a new round trip is measured at R = 120 ms. After the update, what is RTO in milliseconds? (The RTTVAR update uses the SRTT from before the update.)
prompt.zh: 沿用上面的公式：当前 SRTT = 80 ms，RTTVAR = 4 ms，新测到一次往返 R = 120 ms。更新之后，RTO 是多少毫秒？（RTTVAR 的更新用更新之前的 SRTT。）

explain.en: RTTVAR = 0.75×4 + 0.25×|80 − 120| = 3 + 10 = 13; SRTT = 0.875×80 + 0.125×120 = 70 + 15 = 85; RTO = 85 + 4×13 = 137 ms. When a round trip suddenly gets longer, the variation estimate jumps, and the timer leaves more margin.

hints.en: First work out the new RTTVAR, then the new SRTT, and finally RTO = SRTT + 4 × RTTVAR.
hints.zh: 先算新的 RTTVAR，再算新的 SRTT，最后 RTO = SRTT + 4 × RTTVAR。
